understanding.identityScope: Hamilton Khaki Field Murph 42 mm H70605731. Current catalog and 2019 photographs are kept distinct; no claim that all production revisions have identical internals.
learningGoals: Explain the difference between stored power, winding and regulation.
See how independent hands move above a clean stationary dial.
Understand the front and rear transparent windows, housing and sealing interfaces.
Connect visible component appearance to supported materials and general making processes.

references.title: Hamilton H70605731 specifications
references.observation: Current product listing identifies H-10, front sapphire, open back and main dimensions.
references.limitations: No mechanical drawing, internal tolerances, or separately identified rear-window material.

references.title: Hamilton front photograph
references.observation: Inspected front dial, hand profiles, markings, crown and stitching.
references.limitations: Hands obscure some printing; no underside or depth calibration.

references.title: Hamilton dial macro
references.observation: Inspected smooth dial surface, distinct raised hands, crystal reflection and case finishes.
references.limitations: Glare and perspective are not component textures or measurements.

references.title: Hamilton laid-view photograph
references.observation: Inspected case flank, lugs, crown and strap transition.
references.limitations: Different strap pose from the generation input; not calibrated multiview.

references.title: Fratello 2019 Murph rear photograph
references.observation: Inspected window, separate metal ring, slotted perimeter, signed rotor, central bearing, visible bridges and 25-jewel inscription.
references.limitations: 2019 specimen; rotor occludes much of the mechanism. Photo does not prove rear-window composition.

references.title: Fratello first-hand Murph review
references.observation: First-hand exterior review and rear photograph, not a disassembly.
references.limitations: Table says 23 jewels despite its own photograph showing 25; subtype claim is not treated as confirmed. 52 mm lug-to-lug differs from current catalog 53 mm.

references.title: Hamilton H-10 family photograph
references.observation: Inspected rotor, bridges, central pivot, visible balance and gear regions.
references.limitations: Generic family illustration; not proof of every detail in this reference or production year.

references.title: Hamilton automatic/manual watch instructions
references.observation: H-10 is among covered calibers; winding and crown settings are described.
references.limitations: Operating instructions, not an exploded service drawing; functions vary by model.

references.title: FHH mechanical watch explanation
references.observation: Explains stored spring energy, wheel train, escapement and balance regulation.
references.limitations: General mechanism; does not establish H-10 tooth counts, wheel coordinates or tolerances.

references.title: Comadur sapphire components
references.observation: Describes synthetic alumina crystal growth, machining and anti-glare treatments.
references.limitations: No claim that this is the Murph supplier, growth method or coating recipe.

references.title: Swatch Group Nivachron announcement
references.observation: Describes a titanium-based balance-spring alloy and resistance to environmental effects.
references.limitations: Does not establish the spring dimensions or its presence in an arbitrary older specimen.

references.title: RC Tritec luminous pigment application
references.observation: Describes pigment/varnish mixtures and application tools.
references.limitations: Does not identify the Murph pigment grade or Hamilton application process.

references.title: Blancpain first-hand visit to Universo
references.observation: Describes hand stamping and finishing at a manufacturer.
references.limitations: About Blancpain/Universo processes; not evidence of Hamilton sourcing or exact routing.

references.title: Swiss watch industry movement assembly
references.observation: Describes machining, finishing and assembly of mechanical movement components.
